post.headline: Pair technical evidence with a readable summary
post.subtext: Email Validation pairs entered technical details with a short Validation Summary so recipient teams can scan the outcome while preserving the underlying evidence.
post.image_alt_text: A light-mode Hush Line social graphic headed “Pair technical evidence with a readable summary.” It shows the desktop Tools page with the Email Validation tab selected, Raw Email Headers in a text field, Validate Headers and Download Report buttons, and a Validation Summary stating that the email appears to originate from the stated sender. The graphic shows how a readable conclusion is presented with the supporting technical details.

social.bluesky: Email Validation pairs technical details with a short Validation Summary. Recipient teams get a readable outcome while the evidence remains visible for closer examination. The design suits shared work and does not ask everyone to be an email specialist.
social.linkedin:
Email Validation is for more than email specialists.

In Hush Line, Email Validation places a short Validation Summary beneath Raw Email Headers. The detailed input stays visible, while the conclusion is simple for a recipient team to scan.

That design offers a newsroom, school, law office, or community group the same starting point for each person and keeps the technical evidence in view.

Start with the summary for a quick overview. The detailed input remains available for closer examination.
social.mastodon:
Technical email details can have a readable conclusion.

Hush Line’s Email Validation leaves Raw Email Headers visible and places a short Validation Summary below them. A recipient team can scan the outcome and retain the evidence.

Start with the summary, then examine the details as needed.

post.rationale: The required screenshot is a cooldown fallback, so this rewrite moves away from the July post’s pre-action checklist. It uses the design-principle format to focus on accessibility: a readable Validation Summary sits alongside the technical input, helping recipient teams share an understanding without removing the underlying evidence.
